what: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by the E20 lane, and it is ONE ROOT CAUSE BEHIND TWO SEPARATELY-FILED DEAD WATCHDOGS. [!] THE MECHANISM: a session spawned by a Routine firing gets NEITHER a checkout of this repo NOR any mcp__* connector tools. Established by DIRECT OBSERVATION on two independent Routines, not inferred. (a) trig_01MFG5cYsTsS1bci279A2TKi, the lane-watchdog this lane created: fired once deliberately as a smoke test, and get_session on session_01GyB7Zej9GgVoodnfKz4Re5 shows `session_context` carrying NO `sources` and a tool list holding no mcp__* entry; create_trigger had already warned in terms that the trigger 'stores no MCP connectors'. (b) trig_01TWdAvrwFLe6T9XFoNopTeo, the Manager queue watch, which has existed since 2026-09-02: `enabled: true`, cron `56 * * * *`, `last_fired_at` 2026-09-22T12:56:24Z, `last_run.status` SUCCEEDED — and get_session on that firing (session_018tj1rtL2SPANzNwQLhUCei) shows the SAME two absences, plus `mcp_connections: []` on the trigger itself. [!] THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, because an absence is only evidence if the field is emitted when present: get_session on an ORDINARY lane DOES return `sources: [{git_repository: ...}]`, checked against this session's own record in the same minute. So the absence is a real reading rather than a gap in the projection. [!] WHAT IT COST AND WHY NOBODY SAW IT: that Routine's prompt has TWO steps it cannot perform — step 1 needs list_sessions (an mcp__ tool it does not hold) and step 2 needs `python3 scripts/ops/queue_latency.py --write-receipt` from the repo root (a checkout it does not have). So it has fired ~479 times over 479 hours at roughly $0.19 per firing — on the order of $90 — reporting SUCCEEDED every time and writing nothing. Its own guard, scripts/ci/check_manager_queue_watch.py, has been correctly reporting NEVER_RAN_OVERDUE, a state added 2026-09-12 precisely to distinguish 'has not fired yet' from 'has fired ~240 times and written nothing'. THE GUARD WORKED. Nothing acted on it, because NEVER_RAN_OVERDUE deliberately PASSES (only the Routine can clear it) and lands only as a due-list row. [!] THE DISPOSITION ON THE GUARD, ASKED FOR EXPLICITLY AND ANSWERED: DO NOT RETIRE scripts/ci/check_manager_queue_watch.py. It is the only thing in the repo that noticed, its five-state model is correct, and its docstring already anticipated the mcp__ half ('a Routine-fired session holds no mcp__* tools'). What it did not anticipate is the REPO half, which is why its own remedy — step 2 of the Routine prompt — was unperformable. Retiring the guard would delete the detector and keep the defect. [!] THE DECISION OWED IS ABOUT THE ROUTINES, NOT THE GUARDS, and there are only two honest options: EITHER the operator attaches the Claude Code Remote connector AND this repository as a source to each recurring Routine in the claude.ai Routines UI (a session CANNOT do this: connectors on a Routine created through create_trigger are limited to those the calling session can pass through, and a CCR session has none to pass), OR the Routines that cannot be wired are DELETED and the guards that grade them are retired in the same change — `killed` with a stated reason beats a watchdog that bills $90 to report SUCCEEDED while doing nothing. Leaving a third option open (a disabled or unwired Routine still implying coverage) is the state this row exists to end. [!] ONE OPERATOR ACTION FIXES BOTH THIS AND PI-20260922-THE-LANE-WATCHDOG-ROUTINE-FIRES-SESSIONS-WITH-NO-REPO-AND-NO-MCP-SO-IT-IS-DISABLED-AND-THE-INVARIANT-IS-STILL-VOLUNTARY. [!] AND NOTE WHAT WAS NOT EVIDENCE: `enabled: true`, a `next_run_at` in the future, and `last_run.status: SUCCEEDED` are ALL TRUE of this Routine right now. The guard's own docstring already said 'A ROUTINE BEING enabled: true IS NOT EVIDENCE IT FIRES'; the sharper lesson is that FIRING is not evidence it DID anything, because the run succeeds when the agent correctly reports that it cannot do the work.
